buildCommand: node gen/build.mjs && npm --prefix app ci && npm --prefix app run build

rewrites.//: Everything under /app is the SPA and falls through to index.html — EXCEPT the build assets. Without the negative lookahead a hashed bundle that a newer deploy removed does not 404: the rewrite serves index.html in its place, with status 200 and Content-Type text/html, and the browser parses HTML as JavaScript. The result is Unexpected token '<' and a white page, which is what any tab still holding an older index.html gets after a deploy. Excluding assets/ turns that into an honest 404 the console names. The lookahead must be the pattern of a NAMED parameter — Vercel parses source with path-to-regexp, and a bare group carrying the lookahead is accepted at deploy time and then quietly ignored.
